central_question: Why can a burger explain exchange rates better than an abstract formula can hold reader attention?

verified_claims.claim: The Economist publishes Big Mac Index data and calculation code, with source data including local Big Mac prices, exchange rates, GDP and population inputs.
The Big Mac Index is useful as a vivid purchasing-power-parity illustration but not a complete currency valuation model.
Single-product comparisons are memorable but noisy; supporting examples such as latte or furniture prices should be used as illustrations rather than superior models.

useful_numbers_or_examples: Big Mac as a globally recognizable purchasable object
local currency price divided by US-dollar price as implied exchange-rate intuition
myth_or_uncertainty_notes: Do not present a burger as a full PPP basket.
Avoid stale country-specific price claims unless refreshed during later fact-check.
prohibited_or_unsupported_claims: The Big Mac Index predicts exchange rates reliably.
A single burger represents the whole economy.
